title: How old are you?
summary: Ask and give ages with كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ and عُمْرِي … سَنَةً.
intro: Arabic asks 'how much is your age?': كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ (to a man) or كَمْ عُمْرُكِ؟ (to a woman). Answer with عُمْرِي and a number of years. From 3 to 10 the plural سَنَوَات is used, and the number loses its ة because سَنَة is feminine: عَشْرُ سَنَوَاتٍ. From 11 upwards the singular سَنَةً follows: عِشْرُونَ سَنَةً.
objectives: Ask someone's age, to a man and to a woman
Give your age with عُمْرِي … سَنَةً
Say ages from 3 to 10 with سَنَوَاتٍ
Use the round numbers 20 to 70 for older people

realLife.title: Grandma's questions
realLife.story: Sami's grandmother lives with the family. At tea time she sits Daniel next to her and asks how old he is and whether he is married. Everyone laughs, and Daniel learns the ages of the whole family, and which question not to ask.

sentences.literal: how much (is) your age, O Daniel

mistakes.why: From 11 upwards the counted word is singular: سَنَةً, not the plural سَنَوَات.

sentences.en: My brother is ten years old.

mistakes.why: سَنَة is feminine, so a number from 3 to 10 drops its ة: عَشْرُ, not عَشَرَة.

sentences.literal: how much (is the) age (of) your grandfather

sentences.ar: جَدَّتِي كَبِيرَة فِي السِّنّ، عُمْرُهَا سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً.
sentences.en: My grandmother is elderly; she is seventy.
sentences.literal: my grandmother (is) big in the age, her age (is) seventy year(s)

sentences.ar: هَلْ أَنْتَ مُتَزَوِّج؟ لَا، أَنَا لَسْتُ مُتَزَوِّجًا.
sentences.en: Are you married? No, I'm not married.
sentences.literal: (question) you (are) married? no, I am not married

dialogue.title: Grandma asks questions
dialogue.culture: Asking an adult woman her age is usually avoided, as Sami warns. Children, on the other hand, love to be asked, and grandparents are proud of their many أَحْفَاد (grandchildren). Older people are treated with great respect: a guest greets them first and sits where they invite him to.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا يَا ابْنِي! أَنْتَ صَدِيقُ سَامِي الْأَمْرِيكِيّ، صَحِيح؟ اِجْلِسْ هُنَا بِجَانِبِي.
lines.en: Welcome, my son! You're Sami's American friend, aren't you? Sit here next to me.

lines.ar: نَعَم يَا جَدَّتِي، أَنَا دَانْيَال. تَشَرَّفْنَا! بَيْتُكُمْ جَمِيل جِدًّا.
lines.en: Yes, Grandma, I'm Daniel. Nice to meet you! Your home is very beautiful.

lines.ar: شُكْرًا يَا ابْنِي. قُلْ لِي، كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ أَنْتَ شَابّ صَغِير، أَلَيْسَ كَذٰلِكَ؟
lines.en: Thank you, my son. Tell me, how old are you? You're a young man, aren't you?

lines.ar: عُمْرِي عِشْرُونَ سَنَةً، وَسَامِي عُمْرُهُ عِشْرُونَ سَنَةً أَيْضًا، مِثْلِي تَمَامًا.
lines.en: I am twenty years old, and Sami is twenty years old too, exactly like me.

lines.ar: مَا شَاءَ اللّٰه! وَهَلْ أَنْتَ مُتَزَوِّج يَا دَانْيَال؟ عِشْرُونَ سَنَةً عُمْر جَمِيل لِلزَّوَاج!
lines.en: How wonderful! And are you married, Daniel? Twenty is a fine age to get married!

lines.ar: لَا يَا جَدَّتِي، أَنَا لَسْتُ مُتَزَوِّجًا. أَنَا طَالِب، وَلَيْسَ عِنْدِي وَقْت!
lines.en: No, Grandma, I'm not married. I'm a student, and I don't have the time!

lines.ar: جَدَّتِي تَسْأَلُ كُلَّ ضَيْف هٰذَا السُّؤَال يَا دَانْيَال. لَا تَقْلَقْ!
lines.en: My grandmother asks every guest this question, Daniel. Don't worry about it!

lines.ar: وَأَنَا يَا دَانْيَال؟ كَمْ عُمْرِي فِي رَأْيِكَ؟ خَمِّنْ!
lines.en: And what about me, Daniel? How old do you think I am? Guess!

lines.ar: أَنْتِ طِفْلَة ذَكِيَّة جِدًّا… هَلْ عُمْرُكِ عَشْرُ سَنَوَاتٍ، مِثْلَ عُمَر؟
lines.en: You are a very clever child… are you ten years old, like Omar?

lines.ar: لَا! عُمَر عُمْرُهُ عَشْرُ سَنَوَاتٍ، وَأَنَا عُمْرِي ثَمَانِي سَنَوَاتٍ فَقَطْ.
lines.en: No! Omar is ten years old, and I am only eight.

lines.ar: وَأَنْتِ يَا جَدَّتِي، كَمْ عُمْرُكِ، إِذَا سَمَحْتِ؟
lines.en: And you, Grandma, how old are you, if you don't mind my asking?

lines.ar: أَنَا كَبِيرَة فِي السِّنّ يَا ابْنِي: عُمْرِي سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً، وَلِي عَشَرَةُ أَحْفَاد!
lines.en: I'm getting old, my son: I am seventy years old, and I have ten grandchildren!
segs: and I have (lit. and for me)

lines.ar: وَأَبِي عُمْرُهُ خَمْسُونَ سَنَةً، لٰكِنْ لَا تَسْأَلْ أُمِّي عَنْ عُمْرِهَا!
lines.en: And my father is fifty years old, but don't ask my mother how old she is!

lines.ar: فَهِمْتُ! سُؤَالُ الْعُمْر لِلرِّجَال وَالْأَطْفَال فَقَطْ. شُكْرًا عَلَى النَّصِيحَة يَا سَامِي!
lines.en: I understand! The age question is only for men and children. Thanks for the advice, Sami!

reading.title: Ages in Sami's family
reading.ar: فِي بَيْتِ سَامِي سِتَّةُ أَشْخَاص. الْجَدَّة عُمْرُهَا سَبْعُونَ سَنَةً، وَالْأَب عُمْرُهُ خَمْسُونَ سَنَةً. سَامِي عُمْرُهُ عِشْرُونَ سَنَةً، وَعُمَر عُمْرُهُ عَشْرُ سَنَوَاتٍ، وَنُور عُمْرُهَا ثَمَانِي سَنَوَاتٍ.
reading.en: Six people live in Sami's house. The grandmother is seventy years old, and the father is fifty. Sami is twenty, Omar is ten, and Nour is eight.

quiz.prompt: How do you ask a woman 'How old are you?'
How do you say 'I am twenty years old'?
Why does Sami say 'don't ask my mother'?
options: Asking a woman her age is not polite

quiz.prompt: Which word ends in tāʾ marbūṭa (ة)?

completion: Excellent! You can ask and give ages, from a child's to a grandmother's.
